I agree that the usage of this.title or title would be correct, but I do not think it is because Media.title has a protected access modifier. A protected access modifier permits access to the field from within the class itself, from other classes in the package, and any subclasses of the class.

In this case, title is an instance field of Media. Media.title refers to a static field of Media, which does not exist. Instead, using this.title or title would refer to the instance field title of Media.

However, this would only work if Movie is also a subclass of Media.

You may want to consider making your Movie class a subclass of Media, as described in lab task 1. Otherwise, attempting to access the title instance field from the Media superclass may fail (see: https://github.com/klefstad-teaching/lab-1a-clairdelunesolace/pull/1/files#r2677263839).

You should be able to do this using the extends keyword in between the word Movie and the character {. For example:

```java
class Movie extends Media {
```
